algorithms.name: RSA
algorithms.rationale: Relies on the hardness of integer factorization. Shor's algorithm factors integers in polynomial time on a sufficiently large quantum computer, so larger keys raise the quantum resources needed only polynomially and give no lasting protection.

basis.title: Shor, Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Prime Factorization and Discrete Logarithms on a Quantum Computer, SIAM J. Comput. 26(5), 1997

NIST IR 8547 (initial public draft, Nov 2024), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards: lists RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, DH and ECDH as quantum-vulnerable, to be deprecated by 2030 and disallowed by 2035
RFC 8017, PKCS #1 v2.2 (RSA); the 1.2.840.113549.1.1 arc is pkcs-1

algorithms.name: SHA-256
algorithms.rationale: Hash function. NIST defines post-quantum security categories 2 and 4 as the cost of collision search against 256-bit and 384-bit hash functions (SHA-256, SHA-384), i.e. it treats them as the benchmark of quantum-era strength; SHA-512 is larger still.

basis.title: NIST PQC security categories: 1/3/5 are defined by AES-128/192/256 key search, 2/4 by SHA-256/SHA-384 collision search
